title: Systole Increasing Deformations to Maximal Translation Surfaces
summary: A unit-area translation surface is called \emph{maximal} if it maximizes the length of the shortest saddle connection among all surfaces in the same stratum. We investigate whether a non-maximal translation surface can be continuously deformed into a maximal one while the systole increases strictly monotonically. Although such a deformation does not exist in general due to the existence of local but not global maxima of the systole function, we prove that it exists for square-tiled surfaces and translation surfaces obtained from regular hexagons and regular octagons.
